heading: Purpose
text:
### Purpose [LNRE.1.1]

`regex: false` is the setting of the `regex` capability ([LFCA.13.1],
[LCAP.2.8]) that forbids the whole regular-expression surface — `~`,
`!~` and regex literals — in a program and its
libraries. Its purpose: a conforming runtime built for such programs may
omit an RE2-class regex engine entirely ([IRET.23.7]). A program sets it
in its `use` block, or through a dialect that sets it.

RE2 is a substantial, statically-linked matching engine; a build that
never evaluates a pattern carries none of its code, tables, or Unicode
data. A program compiled with `regex: false` trades the ability to write a
regex pattern for the smallest possible runtime image.

Unlike `linear_scan: false` and `logical: false`, `regex: false` changes no runtime
timing: regex evaluation under RE2 is already linear-time and bounded
regardless of pattern ([LREG.9.3]), so there is no T_wcet term to
remove. The payoff is static footprint, not execution cost — see
[LNRE.4.3].
